source_checks.finding: Page confirms the section 'To set the default zoom level for all websites in Microsoft Edge:' with steps Go to Settings and more or press Alt + F; Select Settings and choose Accessibility; Select the desired zoom level from the drop-down menu for Page zoom under Visibility. Page applies to Microsoft Edge on Windows (and Mac). Passage wording is a close paraphrase; the page's exact words for the last step are 'Select the desired zoom level from the drop-down menu for Page zoom under Visibility.' The ref excerpt 'Under "Visibility", choose a zoom level from the "Page zoom" drop-down menu.' is not verbatim; card fix only, not a reason to revise. All claims in the passage are on the page.

Distractor. Page is the desktop Chrome help page ('On your computer, open Chrome'), so the passage is accurate for Chrome on a computer. It does not apply to this Edge on Windows user and is correctly unused in the target. Page section 'Set default page zoom for a specific site' lists Zoom in, Zoom out and Full screen after 'Next to Zoom, choose the zoom options you want:'; wording varied between fetches ('you want' versus 'that you want'), so the ref excerpt is not confirmed word-for-word; card fix only.

required_actions.action: Open the Edge menu with Settings and more, or press Alt + F
Choose a zoom level from the Page zoom drop-down under Visibility, which sets it for all websites

source_checks.finding: Exact sentence confirmed on the desktop Chrome page, in the section for setting page zoom or font size for all webpages (Computer): 'Some websites don't let browsers change only the text size.' Page does not say these sites block page zoom. The user's Ctrl and + is page zoom, so this line is supporting context for why text can stay small, not a stated block on zoom. The target's wording 'For those sites, Chrome can't adjust the font size' is in the passage and is a fair restatement of the page's limit on text-only size changes.

Exact sentence confirmed: 'After you change the zoom levels of sites you've visited, to reset them from one place:'. Steps confirmed on the Computer page: Open Chrome, click More, click Settings; Privacy and security, then Site Settings; Additional content settings, then Zoom levels; to remove resize settings for a specific site, click X. The page says 'resize settings for a specific site' and 'to remove resize settings for a specific site, click X', which supports the target's statement that Chrome keeps a per-site resize setting. The earlier assistant turn's shortcuts are also on this page: Windows and Linux Ctrl and + to zoom in, and Ctrl and - to zoom out.

required_actions.action: Open Chrome Settings, then Privacy and security, Site Settings, Additional content settings, Zoom levels
Find the website in the saved zoom list and click X to remove its resize setting
Know that some websites do not let browsers change only the text size, so Chrome cannot adjust the font size for them

source_checks.finding: Exact sentence confirmed under 'Types of group text messages': 'If any of the recipients aren't using iMessage, then the message is sent as an MMS or SMS.' Page also says 'If all of the recipients are using Apple devices and iMessage is turned on, then the group message is sent as an iMessage.' and 'In iOS 18 or iPadOS 18, you can also send RCS messages.' Page covers iPhone and iPad; the iPhone and iOS 18 applicability in the ref is correct. The target uses only the MMS or SMS sentence, which is on the page.

Exact sentence confirmed: 'If you don't see an option to turn on MMS Messaging, contact your carrier to see if your plan supports Group MMS Messaging.' Steps confirmed: 'In the Settings app, tap Apps, then tap Messages and turn on MMS Messaging.' The page ties MMS Messaging to Group MMS Messaging support, so the target's 'to send group MMS on iPhone, turn on MMS Messaging' is a fair reading. The earlier assistant turn's compose steps are also on this page: 'Open Messages and tap the Compose button', 'Enter the names or tap the Add button', 'Type your message, then tap the Send button'.

required_actions.action: Know that if any recipient is not on iMessage, the group text is sent as MMS or SMS, which explains the Android friend getting separate texts
Turn on MMS Messaging in Settings, Apps, Messages
If there is no MMS Messaging option, contact the carrier to check whether the plan supports Group MMS Messaging
